summary: Plant sterol from soybeans, canola, and wheat germ that inhibits intestinal cholesterol absorption. Structurally similar to cholesterol; contributes to phytosterol blend cholesterol-lowering effects.

name: Sulforaphane
summary: May support detoxification enzymes and reduce oxidative stress.

name: Tanshinone IIA
summary: Tanshinone IIA is a Salvia miltiorrhiza diterpene with cardiovascular mechanistic relevance, but oral isolated human RCT evidence remains unresolved.

name: Taurine
summary: Taurine may support calmness, exercise-fatigue, and cardiovascular contexts without being a direct sedative.

name: Taurine (Sleep Context)
summary: Taurine has insufficient direct human sleep evidence despite plausible inhibitory neurotransmission mechanisms.

name: Taurine Blend
summary: Taurine Blend carries an editorial Grade B rating, but the studies recorded on this profile do not demonstrate that grade. Recorded activity centres on cellular hydration regulation, calcium signaling and cardiac/muscle support, which describes mechanism rather than demonstrated benefit. Safety evidence: human taurine trials report no significant adverse-effect difference from control in studied settings, but this blend formulation is unspecified. Isolated-taurine findings cannot establish the safety of unknown co-ingredients, doses, or long-term use.
evidence_tier: Editorial grade not demonstrated by recorded studies

name: TB-500
summary: TB-500 is a synthetic fragment of thymosin beta-4 marketed for muscle recovery and connective-tissue repair; the underlying Tβ4 biology has real scientific grounding, but the synthetic fragment sold as TB-500 has thin direct human evidence and an unresolved FDA compounding status pending July 2026 PCAC review.

name: Testosterone Boosters Generic
summary: Generic testosterone-booster blends should not be treated as evidence-based; claims must be evaluated ingredient by ingredient, and many products have unsupported claims or dosing below evidence-based levels.

name: Testosterone Support Stack
summary: Testosterone Support Stack is a low-evidence compound profile in the workbook. Keep it in research-hold until PMID/source, safety, and dosage fields are reviewed.

name: tetrandrine
summary: Bisbenzylisoquinoline alkaloid known for calcium-channel-related and NF-κB pathway activity.

name: Theacrine
summary: Theacrine is a purine alkaloid related to caffeine with limited short-term human evidence for energy and mood effects. Evidence remains small-study and supplement-context only.

name: theaflavin
summary: Oxidative black tea polyphenol associated with NF-κB and MAPK pathway effects.

name: theanine
summary: May support relaxation, subjective sleep quality, and some attention outcomes; standalone and caffeine-combination evidence must be separated.

name: thearubigin
summary: Complex black tea polyphenol fraction broadly associated with inflammatory and redox pathway modulation.

name: thujone
summary: Thujone is a monoterpene ketone best known for neuroactive and toxicity-relevant pharmacology in sage- and wormwood-related discussions. Its importance is driven more by receptor-level safety relevance than by positive human efficacy evidence.

name: thymol
summary: Thymol is a monoterpene phenol prominent in thyme and related aromatic herbs. The best-supported effects are antimicrobial and neuroactive membrane-level actions, with little direct clinical evidence for isolated-compound outcomes.
evidence_tier: Editorial grade not demonstrated by recorded studies

name: thymoquinone
summary: Quinone constituent of Nigella sativa with reported NF-κB suppression and Nrf2 signaling support.

name: timosaponin aiii
summary: Steroidal saponin from Anemarrhena asphodeloides (Zhi Mu) associated with anti-inflammatory and neuroprotective activity. Used in TCM; limited isolated human evidence.

name: Tirzepatide
summary: Tirzepatide is a dual GIP/GLP-1 receptor agonist, FDA-approved as Mounjaro and Zepbound, showing the largest average weight-loss effect of any approved obesity drug to date (up to ~22.5% body weight at 72 weeks in SURMOUNT-1) and superior HbA1c reduction versus semaglutide in a head-to-head trial.
primary_effects: Dual GIP and GLP-1 Receptor Agonism
effects: Dual GIP and GLP-1 Receptor Agonism
evidence_tier: Editorial grade not demonstrated by recorded studies

name: Trans-Resveratrol
summary: Trans-resveratrol is the bioactive trans isomer of resveratrol studied for metabolic and vascular biomarkers. Human results are mixed and dose-dependent.
evidence_tier: Editorial grade not demonstrated by recorded studies

name: Trazodone
summary: Trazodone is an antidepressant with serotonergic activity. This profile remains research-only while major-depression efficacy, off-label sleep evidence, cardiac/QT, serotonin-syndrome, orthostatic, priapism, interaction, and regulatory evidence is assembled and reviewed.
primary_effects: serotonin reuptake inhibition and receptor antagonism
effects: serotonin reuptake inhibition and receptor antagonism

name: trigonelline
summary: Alkaloid found in coffee and fenugreek linked to metabolic and neuroprotective effects.

name: Trimethylglycine
summary: Methyl donor that reliably lowers homocysteine biochemically, with uncertain clinical outcome benefit.
evidence_tier: Editorial grade not demonstrated by recorded studies

name: Tryptophan
summary: L-tryptophan has limited human sleep evidence; a 2022 meta-analysis found its clearest pooled signal for reduced wake after sleep onset rather than a broad sleep-latency benefit.

name: TUDCA
summary: Liver enzyme support context; safety screen: bile obstruction without care; pregnancy safety uncertainty.

name: turkesterone
summary: turkesterone carries an editorial Grade B rating, but the studies recorded on this profile do not demonstrate that grade. Recorded activity centres on hormonal signaling context and endocrine, which describes mechanism rather than demonstrated benefit. well tolerated with no significant adverse effects reported.
evidence_tier: Editorial grade not demonstrated by recorded studies

name: Turmeric Curcumin + Piperine
summary: Curcumin plus piperine improves curcumin bioavailability and has moderate evidence for inflammation and osteoarthritis pain outcomes.
evidence_tier: Editorial grade not demonstrated by recorded studies

name: tyrosol
summary: Simple phenolic alcohol from olive oil that provides antioxidant defense and contributes to olive oil's cardiovascular benefits. Works alongside hydroxytyrosol in olive polyphenol health effects.

name: Uc Ii Collagen
summary: Uc Ii Collagen carries a Grade B rating — moderate evidence. Strongest recorded design is a randomized controlled trial, drawn from 2 recorded studies, 2 in people. Recorded activity centres on inflammatory signaling modulation and immune signaling modulation, which describes mechanism rather than demonstrated benefit. Safety evidence: one 180-day trial of a specific undenatured type II collagen product. Safety outcomes did not differ from placebo or glucosamine-chondroitin, but product-source allergy, pregnancy, breastfeeding, autoimmune disease, longer-term use, organ impairment, and medication-interaction safety remain insufficient.

name: umbelliferone
summary: Simple coumarin distributed across Apiaceae with antioxidant-response and MAPK pathway activity.

name: Uracil
summary: Pyrimidine base with biochemical role in RNA synthesis but no supplementation evidence.

name: Uridine Monophosphate
summary: Uridine precursor with limited preliminary evidence for cognitive or phospholipid support.

name: Ursodeoxycholic Acid
summary: Ursodeoxycholic acid (UDCA/ursodiol) is an approved hydrophilic bile acid therapy for cholestatic liver disease. Evidence is strong but disease-specific, especially primary biliary cholangitis.
evidence_tier: Editorial grade not demonstrated by recorded studies

name: Ursolic Acid
summary: Human evidence is insufficient for muscle, fat loss, or metabolic claims; existing support is largely preclinical.

name: Uva Ursi
summary: Uva ursi has limited evidence for urinary symptoms and meaningful safety concerns from arbutin/hydroquinone exposure.

name: valepotriates
summary: Valerian iridoid ester fraction associated with sedative and stress-signaling effects.

name: Valerenic Acid
summary: Valerenic acid is a valerian sesquiterpenoid associated with GABAergic calming effects.
evidence_tier: Editorial grade not demonstrated by recorded studies

name: valerenol
summary: Valerenol is a valerian constituent linked to positive modulation of GABA-A signaling.

name: Valerian Extract (Standardized)
summary: Standardized valerian extract has mixed evidence for sleep quality and should remain limited/inconsistent.

name: Valerian Root Extract
summary: Valerian Root Extract carries a Grade C rating — limited evidence. Strongest recorded design is a meta-analysis, drawn from 2 recorded studies, 2 in people. Recorded activity centres on neurotransmitter modulation, stress response modulation and gabaergic, which describes mechanism rather than demonstrated benefit. Noted cautions include pregnancy/breastfeeding without clinician guidance and children under 12 without medical supervision.

name: Valine
summary: Valine supports muscle metabolism but no strong independent ergogenic effect.

name: verbascoside
summary: Phenylethanoid glycoside (same compound as acteoside) found in Verbascum, Olea, and Plantago species. Anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, and neuroprotective in preclinical models; limited human data.

name: Vinpocetine
summary: Synthetic vincamine derivative with mixed cognitive evidence and U.S. regulatory concerns.

name: Vitamin A
summary: Essential for vision and immune function; excess causes toxicity.

name: vitamin b12
summary: Corrects deficiency and prevents anemia and neuropathy.

name: Vitamin B3
summary: Vitamin B3 is the umbrella nutrient category for niacin forms including nicotinic acid and niacinamide.
evidence_tier: Editorial grade not demonstrated by recorded studies

name: Vitamin B6
summary: PMS symptom support; homocysteine metabolism; safety screen: neuropathy risk with high-dose chronic use.
evidence_tier: Editorial grade not demonstrated by recorded studies

name: Vitamin C
summary: Does not prevent colds in general population but may reduce duration.

name: Vitamin D
summary: Bone health; immune support when deficient; safety screen: hypercalcemia; sarcoidosis; high-dose use without labs.

name: Vitamin D3
summary: May support depressive symptoms in some adults, especially short-term and likely status-context dependent.

name: Vitamin D3 + K2
summary: Vitamin D3 + K2 combines vitamin D repletion with vitamin K-dependent calcium protein activation; sleep evidence is deficiency-dependent and mixed.
evidence_tier: Editorial grade not demonstrated by recorded studies

name: Vitamin E
summary: No mortality benefit; high doses may increase risk.

name: Vitamin K2
summary: May improve bone mineral density and reduce vascular calcification.

name: Whey protein isolate
summary: Muscle protein synthesis; lean mass support; safety screen: milk allergy; severe kidney disease requiring protein restriction.

name: Wild Dagga (Leonotis leonurus)
summary: Wild dagga has insufficient clinical evidence; reported cannabinoid-like effects remain poorly established.

name: Willow Bark Extract
summary: Willow Bark Extract carries a Grade B rating — moderate evidence. Strongest recorded design is a randomized controlled trial, drawn from 2 recorded studies, 2 in people. Recorded activity centres on inflammatory signaling modulation, which describes mechanism rather than demonstrated benefit. Noted cautions include active GI ulcer or reflux disease and asthma with known aspirin or NSAID sensitivity.

name: withaferin a
summary: Reactive withanolide from ashwagandha with strong inflammatory and stress-pathway effects.

name: withanolide a
summary: Steroidal lactone from ashwagandha root with neuroprotective, anti-inflammatory, and anxiolytic properties in animal models. Key bioactive marker in ashwagandha extracts alongside withanolide B.

name: Withanolides
summary: Withanolides are steroidal lactones associated with ashwagandha extracts; human attribution is indirect because clinical studies usually test whole extracts.
evidence_tier: Editorial grade not demonstrated by recorded studies

name: withanoside iv
summary: Steroidal lactone glycoside from ashwagandha associated with neuroregenerative activity.
evidence_tier: Editorial grade not demonstrated by recorded studies

name: wogonin
summary: Wogonin is a flavone associated with Scutellaria research and immune-neuroinflammatory pathway studies. The compound is biologically interesting, but isolated human efficacy evidence remains thin.

name: xanthotoxin
summary: Linear furocoumarin reported from Angelica and parsnip with MAPK and phosphodiesterase-related activity.

name: yangonin
summary: Yangonin is a kavalactone with cannabinoid-related and monoamine-associated signaling.

name: Yellow Dock
summary: Yellow dock contains anthraquinone compounds and has traditional laxative use, but robust human evidence is lacking.

name: Yohimbine
summary: Yohimbine carries a Grade B rating — moderate evidence. Strongest recorded design is a meta-analysis, drawn from 1 recorded study, 1 in people. Recorded activity centres on metabolic regulation, vascular function support and adrenergic, which describes mechanism rather than demonstrated benefit. Noted cautions include severe kidney or liver disease reduces clearance.

name: Zeaxanthin
summary: Retinal antioxidant protection; eye-health stacks; safety screen: none significant; review pregnancy supplement stack.

name: Zinc
summary: Immune support; wound healing support; safety screen: copper deficiency risk with high-dose chronic use; nausea.

name: Zinc Carnosine
summary: Improves gastric mucosal healing and reduces ulcer symptoms.

name: Zinc Picolinate
summary: Zinc picolinate is an absorbable zinc form; sleep evidence is indirect and deficiency-dependent.

name: Zolpidem
summary: Zolpidem is a nonbenzodiazepine sedative-hypnotic medication that positively modulates GABA-A receptor signaling. This profile remains research-only while short-term insomnia efficacy, complex sleep behavior, next-day impairment, CNS-depressant interaction, and regulatory evidence is assembled and reviewed.
